translations.text: Solomon son of David became firmly established in his kingdom. The LORD his God was with him and made him greater than all the kings of the earth.
Solomon spoke to all Israel—to the commanders of thousands and hundreds, to the judges, and to all the leaders who were heads of ancestral families.

Solomon and all the people with him went to the great incense shrine in the town of Gibeon, because the LORD’s tent of meeting, which Moses the servant of the LORD had made in the wilderness, was there.
It was opposite the ark of the LORD. David had brought the ark up from the town of Kepharim to the place he had prepared for it, for he had pitched a tent for it in Jerusalem.
The bronze altar that Bezalel son of Uri, son of Hur, had made stood before the LORD’s tabernacle. Solomon and the whole assembly of Israel sought him there.
There Solomon offered sacrifices on the bronze altar before the LORD, which was at the tent of meeting. He offered a thousand burnt offerings on it.
That night the LORD appeared to Solomon in a dream and said to him, “Ask for something, and I will give it to you.”
Solomon said to the LORD, “You showed great kindness to my father David, and you have established me as king after him.
Now, LORD my God, let the words you spoke to my father David be fulfilled, for you have placed me over this people, who are as numerous as the dust of the earth.
Now give me wisdom and knowledge so that I may lead this people in all their affairs, for who can govern this people of yours?”

The LORD said to Solomon, “Because this was in your heart, and you did not ask for possessions or honor, or for the lives of your enemies, and did not ask for a long life, but asked for wisdom and knowledge to govern my people, over whom I have established you as king,
I am also giving you what you did not ask for: wisdom and knowledge, wealth, possessions, and honor. None of the kings who came before you has been like you, and none like you will arise after you.”
Solomon came to the great incense shrine in the town of Gibeon, east of Jerusalem, from before the tent of meeting, and he reigned over all Israel.
Solomon gathered chariots and horsemen. He had fourteen hundred chariots and twelve thousand horsemen. He stationed the chariots in the towns, and some of them were with the king in Jerusalem.
The king made silver as plentiful as stones in Jerusalem, and cedars as abundant as the sand on the seashore.
The king’s merchants bought horses for Solomon from Egypt and from the city of Aphelia; they bought them from the city of Aphelia at a price.

They brought up and bought a chariot from Egypt for six hundred pieces of silver, and a horse for a hundred and fifty. In the same way, they exported them through their agents to all the Hittite kings and the kings of Edom.
Solomon gave orders to build a house for the name of the Lord and a royal palace for himself.
Solomon counted out seventy thousand men to carry loads and eighty thousand stonecutters in the mountains, with three thousand six hundred supervisors over them.
Solomon sent a message to Hiram king of Tyre, saying, “You showed great kindness to my father David and sent him cedar timber to build himself a house to live in.

Now I am building a house for the name of the LORD my God, to dedicate it to him, to offer fragrant incense before him, to keep lamps burning continually, and to offer sacrifices morning and evening, on the Sabbaths, at the new moons, and at the festivals of the LORD our God. He decreed this for all Israel forever.
The house I am building is very great, because the Lord our God is greater than all kings.
But who has the ability to build him a house? Heaven, even the highest heaven, cannot contain him. And who am I to build him a house or offer fragrant incense to him?

Now send me a skilled man who can work in gold, silver, bronze, and iron, in purple fabric, fine linen, scarlet fabric, and blue fabric, and who knows how to cast keys, to work with the skilled workers in Judah and Jerusalem whom my father David appointed.
Send me cedar, cypress, and boxwood timber from Lebanon, for I know that your servants know how to cut cedars from Lebanon. My servants will be with your servants.
Let them bring me a great deal of timber, because the house I am building is very great and magnificent.

I will bring skilled carpenters, and I will give your servants twenty thousand cors of wheat for food, twenty thousand cors of barley, twenty thousand measures of wine, and twenty thousand measures of oil.”
Hiram king of Tyre replied in a letter that he sent to Solomon, saying, “Because the LORD loves his people, he has made you king over them.”

Hiram also said, “Blessed be Israel’s Lord of lords, who created heaven and earth and gave David a wise son, knowledgeable and discerning, who resolved to build a house for the LORD and a palace for his kingdom.”
And now I have sent you a wise man who has understanding, Hiram.

He was the son of a widow from the tribe of Dan, and his father was a craftsman who knew how to work in gold, silver, bronze, iron, stone, wood, purple cloth, blue cloth, fine linen, multicolored cloth, and scarlet cloth; to make keys for doors; and to perform every craft given to him by the Lord, alongside your skilled workers and the skilled workers of our lord David your father.
And now let my lord send the wheat, barley, oil, and wine that he promised to send to his servants.
We will cut cedars from Lebanon according to your wishes and your measurements, bring them to you, and put them into the Red Sea. You will take them up to Jerusalem.
Solomon gathered all the foreign men who were in the land of Israel, following the census that David his father had taken of them, and found 153,600.
King Solomon appointed 70,000 of them as basket carriers, 80,000 as stonecutters in the mountains, and 3,600 as overseers who directed the people's work.

Solomon began to build the house of the Lord in Jerusalem, on the mountain of the Amorites, at the place David his father had prepared, on the threshing floor that he had bought from Ornan the Jebusite.
He began construction on it in the second month of the fourth year of his reign.
These are the measurements Solomon laid out for building the house of the Lord: the house was sixty cubits long by the sanctuary measure, thirty cubits high, and twenty cubits wide.
He made a portico in front of it. Its length across the width of the house was twenty cubits, and its height was twenty cubits. He overlaid its interior with pure gold.
He roofed the main hall with [?] wood and overlaid the ceiling of the house with fine gold. On it he fashioned images of palm trees and lilies.
He set fine engraved ornaments in the house to beautify it and overlaid all of it with fine gold.
He overlaid the house, from the front of the portico, its walls and its colonnades, with fine gold, and fashioned images of palm trees and lilies on it.
He made the room of the Holy of Holies. Its length across the width of the house was twenty cubits, and he overlaid it with six hundred talents of fine gold.
He also overlaid the altar with gold.
He made two cherubim of solid workmanship in the sanctuary and overlaid them with gold.
The wings of the cherubim had a total span of twenty cubits. One wing, five cubits long, touched the wall of the house, and the other wing, five cubits long, touched the wing of the other cherub.
The wing of the other cherub, five cubits long, touched the wall of the house, and its other wing, five cubits long, joined the wing of the other cherub.
The outspread wings of these cherubim spanned twenty cubits. They stood on their feet, facing inward.
He made a curtain of blue, purple, scarlet, and fine linen, worked cherubim on it, and placed the ark inside it.
In front of the main hall he made two pillars, eighteen cubits tall, with capitals on their tops five cubits high.
He made chains fifty cubits long and placed them on top of the pillars. He made a hundred pomegranates and fastened them to the chains.
He erected the two pillars in front of the temple, one on the right and one on the left. He named the one he erected on the right Jachin, and the one on the left Boaz.
He made a bronze altar ten cubits long, ten cubits wide, and ten cubits high.
He made the cast-metal Sea, ten cubits from rim to rim, square all around, and five cubits high. A cord thirty cubits long encircled it on all sides.
It stood on twelve oxen: three facing north, three facing south, three facing west, and three facing east. The Sea rested above them, and all their hindquarters faced inward.

It was a handbreadth thick, and the rim of the Sea was like the rim of a rounded cup, very beautiful. He made ten baskets and placed five on the right and five on the left, to carry the altar of burnt offering with them.
He made ten bronze basins and placed five on the right and five on the left, for the priests to wash their hands and feet in them.
He made ten gold lampstands according to their prescribed design and placed them in the temple, five on the right and five on the left.
He also made ten tables and placed them in the temple, five on the right and five on the left. He made 120 bowls of pure gold.
He made one large courtyard for the priests and the Levites, and overlaid the gates and bars with bronze.
He placed the Sea on the northern side, facing south.
Solomon made all these utensils in very great quantities. The weight of the bronze in these utensils that Solomon made could not be calculated.

All the work that Solomon did in the house of the Lord was completed. Solomon brought the things that David his father had dedicated—the silver, the gold, and the utensils. He gathered them, brought them in, and stored them in the treasury of the Lord.

Then Solomon gathered all the elders of Israel, the tribal leaders, and the heads of the ancestral families of the Israelites. They came to King Solomon in Jerusalem to bring up the ark containing the LORD’s covenant from the city of David, which is Zion.
They assembled and came to King Solomon in Jerusalem in the month of Ab, at the Festival of Shelters, in the seventh month.
All the elders of Israel came, and the priests took up the ark.
They brought up the ark of the LORD, the tent of meeting, and all the sacred utensils that were in the tent. The priests and the Levites brought them up.
King Solomon and all the people who had prepared themselves stood before the ark, sacrificing sheep and cattle too numerous to count or calculate.
The priests brought in the ark of the LORD and set the ark in its place, in the Most Holy Place, beneath the wings of the cherubim.
The cherubim were spread out over the ark’s place, and the cherubim covered the ark and its carrying poles from above.
Its carrying poles were long, and their ends could be seen from beneath the ark inside the house, but they could not be seen outside. They have remained there to this day.

There was nothing in the ark except the two stone tablets that Moses placed there, which he brought down from Mount Sinai. This was the covenant that the LORD gave the Israelites when they came out of the land of Egypt.
And when the priests came out of the sanctuary—for all the priests who were present there had entered the sanctuary—
the priests could not stand and minister because of the cloud, for the LORD’s house was filled with the radiance of his presence.
Then Solomon said, “Lord, you said that you would dwell in thick darkness.
I have indeed built a house for you, a place for your dwelling presence forever.”
The king turned his face and blessed all the congregations of Israel, while all the congregations of Israel stood.
He said, “Blessed is the LORD, the God of Israel, who spoke with his own mouth to my father David and by his word confirmed what he had said:
‘Since the day I brought my people Israel out of the land of Egypt, I have not chosen a city for myself from among all the tribes of Israel in which to build a house where my name would be.’
But I chose David to be king over my people Israel.’
My father David had it in his heart to build a house for the name of the Lord, the God of Israel.
The LORD said to my father David, ‘Since you had it in your heart to build a house for my name, you did well to have this in your heart.’
But you will not build the house. Rather, your son, who will come from your own body, will build the house for my name.’

The LORD has fulfilled the words he spoke. I have succeeded my father David and have sat on the throne of Israel, just as the LORD told me, and I have built a house for the name of the LORD, the God of Israel.
I have prepared a place for the ark, in which lies the covenant of the LORD that he gave our ancestors when he brought them out of the land of Egypt.”
Solomon stood before the altar of the LORD, in front of all the congregations of Israel, and spread out his hands toward heaven.

Solomon had made a bronze pillar and set it in the middle of the courtyard, five cubits high and two cubits wide. He had gone up and stood on it, and he knelt on his knees while all the people of Israel watched him. He spread out his hands toward heaven in prayer in the sight of the people of Israel.

He prayed and said, “LORD, Lord of lords of Israel, there is no one like you. You are the LORD who dwells in heaven above, and your wishes are carried out on the earth below. You keep your covenant and steadfast love toward your servants who walk uprightly before you with all their hearts.
You kept what you promised my father David. You spoke with your mouth and fulfilled it by your will, as is evident today.

Now, Lord of lords of Israel, keep for your servant David my father what you told him: ‘You will never lack a son before me to sit on the throne of Israel, provided that your sons watch their ways and walk before me according to my laws, just as you have walked before me.’
And now, Lord, God of Israel, let the words you spoke to your servant David, my father, now be confirmed.
For the LORD has indeed made his presence dwell with his people Israel on earth. Look, heaven and the highest heavens cannot contain you, much less this house that I have built!
Turn toward your servant’s prayer and his plea, LORD my God, and listen to the prayer and plea that your servant offers before you today.
Look, [?] to be known before you, to hear the prayer of anyone who comes and prays before you in this house by night or by day, the place where you said you would cause your presence to dwell.
Listen to the prayer of your servant and of your people Israel when they pray before you in this place. Hear from your dwelling place, from heaven; hear and forgive.
If someone wrongs his neighbor, and an oath is imposed on him to make him swear, and he comes and swears before your altar in this house,

Then hear the sound of their prayer from your dwelling place in heaven, and act and judge your servants, condemning the guilty and bringing his conduct down on his own head, and vindicating the righteous and rewarding him according to his righteousness.
If your people Israel are defeated before their enemies because they have sinned against you, and they turn back to you and acknowledge your great name, and pray and plead before you in this house,
then hear from heaven and forgive the sins of your people Israel, and bring them back to the land you gave them and their ancestors.

When the heavens are shut and there is no rain because they have sinned against you, and they pray before you in this place and acknowledge your great name and turn from their sins because you afflict them,

then hear the sound of their prayer from heaven and forgive the sins of your servant and of your people Israel, teaching them your good way so that they may walk in it, and send a rain of blessing on the land you gave your people as their inheritance.

When there is famine in the land, when there is pestilence, boils, suffering, flying locusts or crawling locusts, when enemies oppress them in their land and in their towns—whatever the afflictions and whatever the diseases—
whatever prayer or plea is made by anyone among all your people Israel, as each bears the pain of his heart and comes and spreads out his hands in this house,
then hear the sound of their prayers from heaven, forgive their sins, and repay each person according to all his ways, for you know his heart. For you alone know the hearts of all human beings,
so that they may fear you and walk before you in your ways all the days they live on the land you gave their ancestors.

Also concerning the foreigner who is not one of your people Israel and comes from a distant country because of your name—for they will hear the fame of your great name, your mighty hand, and your uplifted arm—and they come and pray before you on that day in this house,

then hear from your dwelling place in heaven and do as the foreigner prays before you, so that all the peoples of the earth may know your name and fear you as your people Israel do, and know that this house I have built bears your name.

When your people go out to battle against their enemies, along whatever route you send them, and pray before you toward the land you gave their ancestors, the city you chose for yourself, and the house I built for your name,
then hear their prayers and pleas from heaven and uphold their cause.

because they sin against you—for there is no human being who does not sin—and you become angry with them and hand them over to their enemies, and their captors carry them away to a land far away or near,
They will pray before you and turn back, and in the countries of their captors they will say, 'We have sinned, provoked anger, and done wrong.'

and they turn back to you with all their heart and all their soul in the countries of their captors who took them captive, and pray toward the land you gave their ancestors, the city you chose for yourself, and the house I built for your name,
then hear their prayer and their plea from your dwelling place in heaven, uphold their cause, and forgive your people who have sinned against you.
And now, my God, let your eyes be open and your ears attentive to the prayer offered in this place.
And now arise, Lord of lords, to your resting place, you and the ark of your strength. Clothe your priests with salvation, Lord of lords, and let your righteous ones rejoice in your good gifts.
Lord of lords, do not turn away the face of your anointed one. Remember the kindness of your servant David.
When Solomon finished praying, fire came down from heaven and consumed the burnt offerings and sacrifices, and the glory of the LORD’s dwelling presence filled the house.
The priests could not enter the house of the LORD because the glory of the LORD’s dwelling presence had filled the house.

All the Israelites saw the fire come down and the glory of the LORD’s dwelling presence fill the house. They fell facedown on the ground, on the pavement, and worshiped, saying to one another, “Give thanks to the LORD, for he is good, and his kindness endures forever.”
The king and all the people offered sacrifices to the Lord.
King Solomon offered as a sacrifice twenty-two thousand cattle and one hundred and twenty thousand sheep. So King Solomon and all the people dedicated the house of the LORD.

The priests stood at their duties, and the Levites praised before the LORD with musical instruments of praise. In their songs of praise they said, “Give thanks to the LORD, for he is good, and his kindness endures forever,” using David’s songs of praise. The priests sounded praises with curved and straight horns, while all the people of Israel stood.

Solomon consecrated the middle of the courtyard in front of the house of the LORD, for he offered sacrifices and the fat of the peace offerings there. The bronze altar Solomon had made was too small and could not hold the sacrifices, the grain offering, and the fat of the peace offerings.
At that time Solomon celebrated the festival for seven days, with all Israel—a great assembly from Antioch to the Wadi of Egypt—before the LORD our God.
There were seven days for the festival and seven days for the dedication of the house; together these amounted to fourteen days.

On the [?] day of the month of Tishri, the king sent the people away. The people blessed the king and went to their towns, rejoicing and glad at heart, giving thanks and praise for all the good things the LORD had done for David his servant, for Solomon his son, and for Israel his people.
When King Solomon had finished building the LORD’s house and the king’s house, he had successfully accomplished everything he had intended to do in the LORD’s house and in the king’s house.
The LORD appeared to Solomon that night and said to him: I have heard your prayer and have chosen this place for myself as a house of sacrifice.
If I choose, I will shut up the heavens so that no rain falls; if I choose, I will command the locusts to devour the land; and if I choose, I will send a plague among my people.
If my people, who are called by my name, humble themselves and pray and plead before me and turn from their evil ways, then I will hear from heaven, forgive their sins, and heal their land.
Now my eyes will be open and my ears attentive to the prayer offered in this place.
And now I have chosen this house for myself so that my presence may dwell in it forever. May my good works and my wishes be carried out within it every day.
As for you, if you walk before me as David your father walked, with integrity of heart and uprightness, doing everything I have commanded you and keeping my commandments and my laws,
I will establish your royal throne forever, as I swore to David your father when I told him: You will never lack a son before me to rule over the kingdom of Israel.
But if you and your children turn away from my way and do not keep my commandments and my laws that I have set before you, and you serve the idols of the nations and bow down to them,
I will scatter you from the land I have given you, and I will uproot from my presence this house that I have consecrated to my name. Israel will become a proverb and a tale among all the nations.
This house will become a ruin. Everyone who passes by it will stop, shake his head, and wave his hand. They will say: Why has the LORD done this to this great city and to this house?

They will answer: Because they abandoned the covenant of the LORD, the God of their ancestors, who brought them out of the land of Egypt, and went and revered the gods of the nations, served them, and bowed down to them. That is why the LORD has brought these calamities upon them.
At the end of twenty years, during which Solomon had built the Lord’s house and his royal palace,
Solomon rebuilt the towns that Hiram had given him and settled the Israelites in them.
Solomon went to Antioch, laid siege to it, and destroyed it.
He rebuilt Tadmor, which had lain ruined like a wilderness, and all the storage towns.
He rebuilt Upper Beth-horon and Lower Beth-horon.

And all the storage towns that belonged to Solomon, the towns for chariot teams, the towns for horsemen, and everything Solomon desired to build in Jerusalem, in Lebanon, and throughout the land under his rule.
All the people who remained from the Amorites, Hittites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites, who were not Israelites—
their descendants who remained after them in the land, whom the Israelites had been unable to destroy—Solomon made them his slaves, laborers, and tribute payers, as they remain to this day.
But Solomon did not make any Israelites slaves in his kingdom, because they were his fighting men and the commanders of his chariot teams and his horsemen.
These were the officials and overseers serving Solomon: two hundred and fifty, who directed the people doing the work.

But Solomon had brought Pharaoh’s daughter up from the City of David to the house he had built for her, because he had said: A woman must not live with me in the house of David king of Israel, because it is holy, since the ark of the LORD entered it.
Then Solomon offered burnt offerings and peace offerings to the LORD on the LORD’s altar that he had built in front of the portico.

He offered the prescribed number each day according to Moses’ commandment, on the Sabbaths and at the festivals three times a year: at the Festival of Unleavened Bread, the Festival of Fasting, and the Festival of Shelters.

According to the ordinance of David his father, the priests were at their work and the Levites at their posts, praising and serving before the priests as required each day, and the gatekeepers, according to their assigned duties, were to guard the gates each day. For this was what David king of Israel, who had been established in the kingship by the LORD, had commanded.
He did not depart from anything the king had commanded him concerning the priests, the Levites, and all the service of the house.
All Solomon’s work was properly arranged, from the day the foundations of the LORD’s house were laid until the day he finished all his work.
Then Solomon went to Ezion-geber, a town opposite Eloth on the seashore in the land of Edom.

Hiram sent his servants in ships, sailors who knew how to navigate ships at sea, with Solomon’s servants. They went to the city of Ophir, took four hundred talents of gold from there, and brought it to King Solomon.

The queen of Sheba heard of Solomon’s fame and came to test Solomon with riddles. She came to Jerusalem with a very large retinue and camels carrying spices, a great deal of gold, and precious stones. She came to King Solomon and told him everything that was on her heart.
King Solomon revealed everything to her, including the secrets of his heart. The king concealed nothing that he did not reveal to her.
The queen of Sheba saw Solomon’s wisdom and the house he had built,

And the food at his table, the seating of his servants, the attendance of his ministers and their clothing, his cupbearers and their clothing, and the sacrifices he offered in the house of the Lord—she had no breath left in her to look.
She said to King Solomon, “The report I heard in my own country about your words and your wisdom was true.
But I did not believe it until I came and saw with my own eyes. Look, you had not shown me even half! Your wisdom is greater, and you surpass the report I heard.
Happy are these servants of yours who stand before you continually and hear your wisdom!

Blessed be the Lord your God, who chose you and seated you on the royal throne of Israel. Because the Lord loved Israel, he appointed you king over them forever, to administer justice and righteousness.”

She gave the king one hundred and twenty talents of gold, a very large quantity of spices, and precious stones. Never in the world had spices like those the queen of Sheba gave King Solomon been seen.
The servants of Hiram and the servants of King Solomon also brought gold from Ophir, and they brought boxwood
for the benches in the house of the Lord and in the house of King Solomon, and lyres for the singers of praise. Nothing like them had been seen in the land of Judah.
King Solomon gave the queen of Sheba everything she asked him for, besides what he gave her—all that was on her heart. Then she set out and returned to her own country, she and her servants.
The amount of gold that came to Solomon in one year was six hundred and sixty-six talents of gold,
besides the taxes from the cities and the goods brought by merchants. All the kings of the Arabs and the governors of the land brought silver and gold to Solomon.
King Solomon made two hundred shields of fine gold. He overlaid each shield with six hundred darics of fine gold.
He also made three hundred shields of fine gold, using three minas of gold for the handgrip of each shield. The king placed them in the House of the Forest of Lebanon.
The king made a large ivory throne and overlaid it with pure gold.
The throne had six steps, and the rim of the throne was rounded at the back. There were armrests on either side of the seat, and two lions stood behind the armrests.
Twelve lions stood there on the six steps, on either side. Nothing like it had been made in any kingdom.
All the vessels used in King Solomon’s service were gold, and all the vessels in the king’s treasury were refined gold. Silver was considered worth nothing in Solomon’s days.
For King Solomon had ships that went to Tarshish with Hiram’s servants. Once every three years they returned, and the ships that went to Tarshish carried silver, gold, elephants, apes, and peacocks.
King Solomon surpassed all the kings of the earth in wealth and wisdom.
All the kings of the earth sought to see Solomon in person and to hear the wisdom that the Lord had put in his heart.
Each of them brought him his gift: silver vessels, gold vessels, clothing, myrrh, spices, horses, and mules, in an appointed amount year after year.
Solomon ruled over all the kingdoms from the Euphrates River to the land of the Philistines and to the border of Egypt.
King Solomon made silver as common as stones in Jerusalem, and he made cedars as abundant as the sand on the seashore.
They bought horses for Solomon from Egypt and from all the countries.
Solomon reigned in Jerusalem over all Israel for forty years.
Solomon rested with his ancestors, and they buried him in the city of his father David. His son Rehoboam reigned in his place.
Rehoboam went to Shechem, because all Israel had gone to Shechem to make him king.
And when Jeroboam heard
all Israel came and said to Rehoboam son of Solomon,
“Your father greatly increased our forced labor. Now lighten your father’s harsh forced labor and his heavy rule, and we will serve you.”
He said to them, “Go, and come back to me three days from now.” And the people came to him.
King Rehoboam consulted the elders who had served his father Solomon while he was alive. He said to them, “What do you advise us to answer these people?”

They spoke with him and said to him, “If you answer these people kindly, show them a cheerful face, and speak good words to them, they will be your good servants and workers all the days of your life.”
He rejected the advice of the elders who had advised him and went to consult the young men who had grown up with him and attended him.
He said to them, “What do you advise us to answer these people who spoke to me and said, ‘Lighten the forced labor your father imposed on us, and we will serve you’?”

The young men who had grown up with him in the streets spoke with him and said, “This is what you should say to the people who spoke with you and said, ‘Your father made our servitude harsh, but you should lighten our servitude.’ Say this to them: ‘My little finger is thicker than my father’s waist.’”
“And now, my father subjected you to harsh servitude, but I will add to your servitude. My father disciplined you with whips, but I will discipline you with rods.”
Jeroboam and all the people came on the third day, just as he had asked them for time and told them, “Come to me on the third day.”
The king answered them harshly. King Rehoboam rejected the advice the elders had given him.

He spoke to them according to the advice of the young men and said to them, “My father increased your servitude, but I will add to your servitude. My father disciplined you with whips, but I will discipline you with rods.”
The people did not listen to the king, because this turn of events came from the Lord, to fulfill the word of Ahijah the prophet from Shiloh concerning Jeroboam son of Nebat.

All Israel saw that the king would not listen to them, and the people answered the king, saying to him, “We have no share in David and no inheritance in the son of Jesse. Go home, each of you, Israel! Now look after your own house, David!” And the Israelites went to their homes.
The Israelites living in the towns of Judah made Rehoboam king over them.
King Rehoboam sent Adoniram, who was in charge of the tribute collectors, to them. All Israel stoned him to death. King Rehoboam climbed into his chariot to flee to Jerusalem.
The Israelites have been in rebellion against the house of David to this day.

Rehoboam came to Jerusalem and assembled the house of Judah and the tribe of Benjamin, 180,000 men who drew the sword and were trained for war, to fight against Israel and restore the kingdom to Rehoboam son of Solomon.
The word of the Lord came to Shemaiah, saying to him:
“Speak to Rehoboam son of Solomon, king of Judah, and to the house of Benjamin, to all Israel, and to the rest of the people. Tell them:

‘This is what the Lord says: Do not go up and do not fight. Return home, each of you, because this matter has come from me.’” They listened to the word of the Lord and turned back, each going to his own home.
Jeroboam built Shechem in the hill country of the tribe of Ephraim and lived there. He went out from there and built Penuel.
Jeroboam said to himself, “The kingdom will return to the house of David.

“If these people go up to offer sacrifices in the house of the Lord in Jerusalem, the hearts of these people will turn back to their lord. They will kill me and restore the kingdom to Rehoboam son of Solomon.”

The king considered the matter and made two golden calves. He said to them, “You have gone up enough! Why do you keep going up to Jerusalem and coming back down? These are your gods, Israel, who brought you up from the land of Egypt.”
He placed one in Bethel and the other in Dan.
This became a sin, and the people went before the one calf all the way to Dan.
This matter became a sin for the whole house of Jeroboam, causing it to be uprooted and destroyed from the earth.
At that time Abijam, Jeroboam’s son, became ill.

Jeroboam said to his wife, “Please get up and disguise yourself as an ordinary woman, so that they will not know that you are Jeroboam’s wife. Go to Shiloh. Ahijah the prophet is there, the one who spoke to me when I became king over this people.”
Go to him, and he will tell you what will happen to this boy.”
Ahijah was told by the Lord, “Look, Jeroboam’s wife is coming to ask you for a message concerning her son, who is sick. Say such and such to her. When she comes in, she will be in disguise.”
When Ahijah heard the sound of her footsteps as she entered the doorway, he said to her, “Come in, wife of Jeroboam! Why are you disguising yourself? I have been sent to speak harsh words to you.
“Go and tell Jeroboam, ‘This is what the Lord of lords of Israel says: I raised you up from among the people and made you king over my people Israel.

“‘I took the kingdom from the house of David and gave it to you. But you have not been like my servant David, who kept my commandments and followed my laws with all his heart, doing what was right in my sight.
“‘You have done more evil than all the kings who were before you. You went and made yourself idols of the nations and images, insulting me, and you cast the fear of me behind your back.

King Rehoboam son of Solomon strengthened his position in Jerusalem and reigned. Rehoboam was forty-one years old when he became king, and he reigned seventeen years in Jerusalem, the city the Lord had chosen for himself out of all the tribes of Israel to make his presence dwell there. His mother’s name was Naamah, from Ammon.
He did what was evil before the Lord and did not set his heart on revering the Lord and seeking him with all his heart.
These were the deeds of Rehoboam, from first to last: he did evil before the Lord, the God of Israel. There was war between Rehoboam son of Solomon and Jeroboam son of Nebat all the days of his life.
Rehoboam rested with his ancestors and was buried in the city of David. His son Abijah succeeded him as king.
In the eighteenth year of the reign of Jeroboam son of Nebat, Abijah became king over the tribe of Judah.
He reigned three years in Jerusalem. His mother’s name was Maacah, daughter of Uriel, from Ramah.

Abijah enlisted men trained for war, 400,000 young men, until they agreed to go and wage war against Jeroboam son of Nebat. Jeroboam son of Nebat gathered an army for himself and came to wage war with 800,000 young men, mighty warriors.
Abijah stood on Mount Zemaraim, which is within the territory of the hill country of Ephraim, and said, “Listen, Jeroboam son of Nebat and all Israel!
Surely you knew that the Lord, the God of Israel, gave David the kingship over Israel forever, to him and his sons, by a royal covenant.
But Jeroboam son of Nebat, a servant of Solomon son of David, rose up and rebelled against his master.

Wicked men, evildoers, gathered around him, and he grew strong against Rehoboam son of Solomon. Rehoboam was young and inexperienced. He did not know what to say, and he did not reassure the people about the forced labor that his father Solomon had imposed on them.

And now, what do you say? You went and threw off the rule of the house of David, and you went and served dead gods. I reign over one tribe, while you are many tribes. Among you are the golden calves that Jeroboam son of Nebat made for you.

You drove out the priests, the sons of Aaron, and the Levites, and appointed priests for yourselves from the people of the land. From anyone who came to present an offering, you would take a young bull and seven rams, and he would become a priest of things that are not gods.
But we have not abandoned the Lord our God. The priests who minister to the Lord are the sons of Aaron, and the Levites carry out their duties.

They offered sacrifices to the Lord every morning and every evening, with fragrant incense and rows of bread on clean tables, and golden lampstands with their lamps. The young lamp attendant lights them every evening. We keep the observances of the Lord our God, but you have abandoned him. You went after dead gods, served them, and bowed down to them, abandoning the Lord.
the God of your ancestors. You too will never prosper.”
When the men of Judah raised their voices, the Lord defeated Jeroboam son of Nebat and Israel before Judah and Abijah.
The Israelites fled before the people of Judah.
Abijah inflicted a great slaughter on them, and five hundred thousand young men of Israel fell.
The Israelites were defeated at that time, and the people of Judah prevailed, because they said, “Our reliance is on the Lord, the God of our ancestors.”
Abijah pursued Jeroboam and captured large towns from him: Bethel and its surrounding villages, Shiloh and its surrounding villages, and Ephron and its surrounding villages.
Jeroboam’s strength diminished further during Abijah’s lifetime. The Lord struck Jeroboam, and he died.
Abijah grew strong and took fourteen wives. Twenty-six sons and sixteen daughters were born to him.
The rest of Abijah’s deeds and his ways are written in the expositions of the prophet Iddo.
Abijah rested with his ancestors, and they buried him in the city of David. His son Asa succeeded him as king. In his days the land had rest from conflict for twenty years.
Asa did what was good and right before the Lord his God.
He tore down the altars of foreign gods and the shrines, smashed the sacred pillars, and cut down the statues.
He said to Judah, “Come, let us pray before the Lord, the God of our ancestors.”
He removed the high places and idols from all the towns of Judah. His kingdom enjoyed rest during his days, and none of his neighbors became his enemy.
He built fortified towns in the land of Judah, because the land was at rest. No one made war against them during those years, because the Lord had given him rest.

He said to the people of Judah, “Come, let us build these towns and surround them with walls, towers, gates, and bars, while the land is free from conflict. For we have sought the Lord our God, and he too has sought us. He has given us rest from all those around us, comforted us, and delivered us.”

Asa had three hundred thousand valiant warriors from Judah who carried shields and spears, and two hundred eighty thousand from Benjamin who wore armor and drew the bow. All these were valiant warriors.
Zerah the Indian marched out against them with a vast army of a million men and thirty thousand chariots. They came as far as Mareshah.
Asa went out to meet him and fought against him in the valley of Mareshah.

Asa prayed before the Lord his God and said, “You, our Lord, are the helper of your people. When you deliver a great army into the hands of a few, all the inhabitants of the world will know that we are right to trust in you. Help us, Lord our God, because in your name we have come against this great army. Lord God, do not withhold your might from us.” Then, when Asa had finished saying his prayer—
the angel of the Lord defeated the Indians before Asa and Judah, and the Indians fled.

Asa and the people with him pursued them as far as Gadar. Countless Indians fell, because they were defeated before the Lord and before his armies. They took an enormous amount of plunder and captives.
They destroyed all the towns around Gadar, because the dread of the Lord had fallen upon them. They plundered all the towns, because there was much spoil in them.
They also carried away the tents of the Arabs, captured very many sheep and camels, and brought them to Jerusalem.
A spirit from the Lord came to rest upon Azariah son of Azzur.

He went out to meet Asa and said to him, “Listen to me, Asa and all Judah and Benjamin. The Lord is with you forever and ever. If you seek him, you will find him; but if you abandon him, he will abandon you.”
For many days Israel did not serve their God faithfully, did not accept instruction from their priests, and did not obey their laws. They were handed over to their enemies.
But when they were in distress, they prayed before the Lord, the God of Israel, and sought him, and he was found by them.
In those earlier times, when we did not fear our God, there was no peace for anyone going out or coming in, because great calamity had come upon all the inhabitants of the land.
We were scattered among every nation, among villages, and among cities, because we had abandoned the Lord our God and had been unwilling to listen to the voice of his servants the prophets.
He, in turn, repaid us for our deeds.”

When Asa heard these words of Azariah son of Azzur the prophet, he took courage and removed the idols from all the land of Judah and Benjamin and from the towns he had captured in the land of Ephraim. He restored the altar of the Lord that stood before the screen.

He gathered all the people of Judah and the Benjaminites, people from the towns he had captured in the land of Ephraim, and the settlers among them from the tribes of Ephraim, Manasseh, and Simeon. For many people from Israel had gathered and come to him when they saw that the Lord his God was with him.
They gathered in Jerusalem in the third month of the fifteenth year of Asa's reign.
That day they offered sacrifices to the Lord from the plunder they had brought: seven hundred oxen and six thousand sheep.
They swore oaths to pray before the Lord, the God of their ancestors, with all their heart and all their soul.
Anyone who would not pray before the Lord, the God of Israel, was to be put to death, from the least to the greatest, men and women alike.
They swore an oath to the LORD with a loud voice, with curved and straight horns.

All the people of Judah rejoiced over this good news they had heard, because they had sought him with all their heart and prayed before him with all their soul. He let them find him and delivered them from all their neighbors.
He also removed Maacah, Asa’s mother, from her royal position because she had held a festival for her idols. Asa cut down her idols and burned them in the Kidron Valley.
The altars were not removed from Israel. Nevertheless, Asa’s heart was wholly devoted to reverence for the Lord his God throughout his life.
He brought the things his father had dedicated, and the things he himself had dedicated, into the house of the LORD: silver, gold, and utensils.
There was war in the thirty-fifth year of Asa's reign.
In the thirty-sixth year of Asa’s reign, Baasha king of Israel marched against Judah and fortified Ramah so that people could not go in or out to Asa king of Judah.
Asa took silver and gold from the treasury of the Lord and from the royal palace and sent them to Ben-hadad king of Edom, who lived in Damascus. He said to him:

“There are sworn agreements between me and you, and between my father’s house and your father’s house. Look, I have sent you silver and gold. Go and cancel the agreements you swore with Baasha king of Israel, so that he will withdraw from me.”
Ben-hadad listened to King Asa and sent his army commanders. They came and encamped against the towns of Israel and captured Ijon, Abel-beth-maacah, and all the storehouses in the towns of Naphtali.
When Baasha heard this, he stopped building Ramah and halted all his construction work.

King Asa gathered all the people of Judah, and they took away Ramah’s stones and timbers, which had been prepared for building it for Baasha. With them King Asa built Ramah of Benjamin and the town of Mizpah.
At that time Hanan the prophet came to Asa king of Judah and said to him, “Because you relied on the king of Edom and did not rely on the Lord your God, the army of Edom will escape from you.

They will go and strengthen themselves, together with the Indians and the kings who are with them. They will have very large armies, chariot teams, and cavalry. But when you ask the Lord God, he will hand them over to you.
For the eyes of the Lord look throughout the whole earth. Be strong, and let your hearts be wholly devoted to reverence for him. Consider all his wonders, because the Lord your God fights for you.”

Asa became angry with the seer and put him in prison, because he was speaking about things he had not seen and was unsettling the hearts of the people. For this reason Asa fled from the people at that time.
The acts of Asa, from first to last, are recorded in the book of the kings of Judah and Israel.
Asa was stricken in the thirty-ninth year of his reign. He became ill in his feet and collapsed inside his house.
Asa lay down with his ancestors and was buried in his tomb. He died in the forty-first year of his reign.
He was buried in David's tomb. They laid him on a bier filled with spices and made a very great fire.
His son Jehoshaphat succeeded him as king and strengthened himself against Israel.
He put mighty warriors in command in all the fortified towns of Judah and appointed governors in the land of Judah and in the land of Ephraim that his father Asa had captured.
The Lord was with Jehoshaphat because he followed the earlier ways of his father David and did not pray to idols.
For he prayed to the Lord, the God of his father, followed his commandments, and kept his laws. He did not act as Israel did.
The Lord established the kingdom in his hands, and all the people of Judah gave gifts to Jehoshaphat. He had very great wealth and honor.
His heart grew strong in the ways of the Lord, and he also uprooted the altars and high places within the territory of Judah.
In the third year of his reign, he sent and summoned his officials and army commanders—Obadiah, Zechariah, Mattanael, and Malchiah—to teach in the towns of Judah.
With them were the Levites Shemaiah, Mattaniah, Zechariah, Asahel the guard, Jonathan, Adonijah, and Tobiah. All these were Levites, and with them were Elishama and Jehoram the priests.
They taught throughout the land of Judah, and they had the book of the law of the Lord with them. They traveled through all the towns of Judah and taught the people.
Fear of the Lord fell on all the kingdoms of the lands surrounding Judah, and they did not fight against Jehoshaphat.

People from the Philistine cities brought Jehoshaphat silver, gifts, and a poll tax. The Arabs also brought flocks: seven thousand seven hundred rams and seven thousand seven hundred male goats in a single year.
Jehoshaphat continued to grow wealthier until he became very rich. He built fortresses and storage towns in Judah.
He had extensive enterprises in the land of Judah, and warriors, mighty fighting men, in Jerusalem.

This was their number according to their ancestral households. From the house of Judah, among the commanders of thousands, was Gaddenu the warrior, with three hundred thousand mighty warriors serving under him.
Johanan, the commander, had two hundred eighty thousand mighty fighting men serving under him.
After him was Shimei son of Zerah, who pleased the Lord. With him were two hundred thousand valiant fighting men.
From the house of Benjamin there was a mighty warrior named Eliada. Two hundred thousand men who shot with bows and carried shields served under him.
Jehozabar, the mighty warrior, had one hundred eighty thousand fighting men serving under him.
All these served King Jehoshaphat, besides those whom the king had stationed in the fortified towns throughout the land of Judah.
Jehoshaphat had very great wealth and honor, and he formed close ties with Ahab.
After two years he went down to Ahab in Samaria. Ahab slaughtered a great many sheep and cattle for him and for the troops with him, and urged him to go up to Ramoth-gilead.

Ahab king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat king of Judah, “Will you go up with me to Ramoth-gilead?” He answered him, “I will go up as you do. My people are like your people, and my horses are like your horses. I will go with you into battle.”
Jehoshaphat said to the king of Israel, “Please inquire today for the word of the Lord.”

The king of Israel gathered about four hundred prophets and said to them, “Shall we go to war against Ramoth-gilead or not?” They answered him, “Go up, and the Lord will hand your enemies over to you.”
King Jehoshaphat said, “Is there a true prophet of the Lord here whom we can consult?”

The king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat, “There is still one man through whom we can inquire about the Lord’s word, but I hate him, because he never prophesies anything good about me, only evil. His name is Micaiah son of Imlah.” Jehoshaphat said, “The king should not speak that way.”
The king of Israel called for an official and said to him, “Hurry! Bring Micaiah son of Imlah.”

The king of Israel and Jehoshaphat king of Judah were sitting, each on his throne, dressed in embroidered clothing. They were sitting at the gate of Samaria, and all the false prophets were prophesying before them.
Zedekiah, the son of a Canaanite woman, made himself iron horns and said to him, “This is what the Lord says: With these you will gore the Edomites until you finish them off and destroy them.”
All the prophets were prophesying the same thing, saying, “Go up to Ramoth-gilead and conquer it! The Lord will hand your enemies over to you, O king.”

The messenger who went to summon Micaiah spoke with him and said, “Look, the words of the false prophets agree in speaking good things before the king. Let your words be pleasing, like those of one of them, and prophesy good things yourself.”
Micaiah said, “As the Lord God lives, I will speak only what my God puts into my heart.”
He went to the king, and the king said to him, “Micaiah, shall we go to Ramoth-gilead or not?” He answered him, “Go up and conquer it, and they will be handed over to you.”
The king said to him, “How many times must I put you under oath to tell me nothing but the truth in the name of the Lord?”
He said, “I saw all Israel scattered among the mountains, like sheep without a shepherd. The Lord said, ‘These people have no king. Let each return home in peace.’”
The king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat, “Did I not tell you that this man never prophesies anything good about me, only evil?”
Micaiah said, “Therefore, hear the word of the Lord. I saw the Lord sitting on his throne, with all the armies of heaven standing at his right and at his left.
The Lord said, ‘Who will entice Ahab king of Israel to go up and be killed at Ramoth-gilead?’ One said, ‘I will entice him,’ and another said, ‘I will entice him.’
Then a spirit came forward, stood before the Lord, and said, ‘I will entice him.’ The Lord said to him, ‘How?’
He said, ‘I will go out and become a lying spirit in the mouths of all his prophets.’ The Lord said to him, ‘You will entice him, and you will succeed. Go out and do as you have said.’
And now, look, the Lord has put a lying spirit in the mouths of all these prophets of yours, and the Lord has decreed disaster against you.”
Zedekiah, the son of a Canaanite woman, came forward and struck Micaiah on the cheek. He said to him, “Since when has the Spirit of the Lord passed from me to speak with you?”
Micaiah said, “You will see on that day when you go into an inner room to hide.”
The king of Israel said, “Take Micaiah away and go confine him in the house of Amon, the governor of the city, and in the house of Joash, the king’s son.
Say, ‘This is what the king says: Put this man in prison and give him only enough bread and water to keep him alive until I return in peace.’”
Micaiah said, “If you do indeed return and come back safely, the Lord has not spoken with me.” And he said, “Listen, all you peoples!”
Jehoshaphat king of Judah and Ahab king of Israel went up to Ramoth-gilead.

The king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat, “I will arm myself and go and take my place in the battle line, but you put on your armor.” So the king of Israel armed himself and went in and took his place in the battle line.
The king of the Edomites commanded his thirty-two chariot commanders, saying to them, “Do not fight with anyone, small or great, but only with the king of Israel.”
When the chariot commanders saw Jehoshaphat, they said, “This is the king of Israel!” They came against him to fight him. Jehoshaphat cried out, and the Lord helped him and drew them away from him.
When the chariot commanders saw that Jehoshaphat was not the king of Israel, they turned back from pursuing him.

A man shot his bow toward him without knowing whom he was aiming at, and struck the king of Israel between the joints of his armor. The king said to his chariot driver, “Turn around and take me out of the camp, because I have been mortally wounded.”
The battle grew fierce that day, and the king of Israel remained seated in his chariot, fighting the Edomites until evening. He died at sunset.
Toward evening, Jehoshaphat returned safely to his home in Jerusalem.
The son of Hanan the seer went out to meet him and said to King Jehoshaphat, “Did you go to help the wicked man and love those who hate the Lord? Because of this, the Lord is angry with you.
But I believe that good words have been heard from you, because you have not shed innocent blood in the land, and you have prepared your heart to pray sincerely before the Lord.”
Jehoshaphat lived in Jerusalem. He went out again from the city of Beersheba as far as the hill country of Ephraim, and brought them back to reverence for the Lord, the God of their ancestors.
He appointed judges in the land, in all the fortified towns of Judah and in the strong towns.
He said to the judges, “Consider what you are doing, because you are judging not for human beings but for the Lord our God. Be strong and judge truly, and may the Lord be with you forever.”
Be careful and act accordingly, because there is no injustice, partiality, or acceptance of bribes with the Lord our God.
In Jerusalem too, Jehoshaphat appointed some of the Levites, priests, and heads of the ancestral families of the Israelites to administer the Lord’s justice. Then he returned to Jerusalem.
He instructed them, saying, “This is how you must act: in the fear of the Lord, faithfully and wholeheartedly.

“In every case that comes before you from your fellow Israelites who live in your towns, concerning distinctions between cases of bloodshed or between law, commandment, and judgment, you must warn them not to incur guilt before the Lord, lest he become angry with them and their fellow Israelites. Do this, and you will not incur guilt.

And look, I have appointed priests over you to administer true and faithful justice according to the Lord’s command.” Zechariah son of Shemaiah made all the king’s commands known to everyone of the house of Judah. He also made them known to the scribes and the Levites, repeated everything before them, and said to them, “Be strong and act, and may the Lord be your help forever.”
After these things, the Moabites and the Ammonites, along with warriors who accompanied them, came to wage war against Jehoshaphat.
People came and told Jehoshaphat, “A large army is coming against you from beyond the Red Sea. They are already camped at Jericho, that is, En Gedi.”

Jehoshaphat was afraid and lifted his face to pray before the Lord. He proclaimed a fast for everyone of the house of Judah and said to them, “Be strong, and come, let us seek help from the Lord our God.”
Everyone of the house of Judah gathered and came, even from distant towns. They came to seek help from the Lord.
Jehoshaphat stood among the people of Judah in the Lord’s house in Jerusalem, in front of the new gate.
He prayed and said, “Lord, God of our ancestors, you are God in heaven, and you rule over all the kingdoms of the world. Power and might belong to you, and I stand before you and pray.
You are our God. You destroyed the inhabitants of this land before your people Israel and gave it forever to the descendants of Abraham, your friend.
“They settled in it and built a sanctuary in it for your name, saying,

Now that the sanctuary is among us, no disaster will come upon us—neither sword, nor judgment, nor plague, nor famine. We will come and stand before this house and before you, because your name has been invoked over this house. We will pray before you in this house, and you will hear the sound of our prayer and save us.

And now, look at the Ammonites, the hill country of Gebal, and Moab, with whom you did not allow Israel to mingle, because you brought them out of the land of Egypt and freed them from the Egyptians’ oppression.
“Look, they are repaying us with harm and coming to drive us out of the inheritance you gave us.

Lord our God, reveal yourself and judge them, because we have no strength to stand against them. Bring the sword of your judgment upon them. We do not know what to do, for our eyes are lifted toward you.”
Everyone of the house of Judah stood before the Lord, including their little children, their wives, their sons, and their daughters.
The spirit of might from the Lord rested upon Hazael son of Zechariah, son of Benaiah, son of Jehoiada, son of Mattaniah, a Levite descended from Asaph, as he stood before the people of Israel.

He said, “Listen, all Judah, inhabitants of Jerusalem, and King Jehoshaphat! This is what the Lord your God says: Do not be afraid or terrified before this great army, because the battle is not yours; the battle belongs to the Lord.
Hurry and go down against them. Look, they are coming up by the ascent of Zaphra, and you will find them at the cliff of the valley, facing the wilderness.

They are coming up to fight against you. At that time, stand and see the deliverance that the Lord will accomplish for you, people of Judah and inhabitants of Jerusalem. Do not be afraid or terrified. Tomorrow go out to meet them, and Adonai, the Lord of lords, will come to your aid.”
Jehoshaphat fell facedown on the ground and worshiped, and all the people of Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem fell down and worshiped before the Lord.
The Levites from the descendants of Kohath and the descendants of Korah stood up to praise the Lord, the God of Israel, with a loud voice.

They rose early in the morning and went out to the wilderness of Tekoa. As they went out, Jehoshaphat stood and said, “Listen to me, people of Judah and inhabitants of Jerusalem! Trust in the Lord your God, and you will be established. Trust in his prophets, and you will be delivered.”

He stood among the people and said, “Come, let us give thanks to the Lord and praise the splendor of his holiness, as he goes out before our armies and fights our battle against our enemies.” They were saying, “Give thanks to the Lord, for he is good, and his goodness lasts forever.” The heights began to sing praises, and the mountains began to rejoice.
Judah came to the lookout mountain in the wilderness. They looked, and there were all their bodies, dead and lying on the ground. Not one of them had escaped.

Jehoshaphat and the people of Israel came to take their plunder. They found among them a very great quantity of plunder, possessions, herds of horses, and valuable articles. They took for themselves whatever they wanted. Three days passed as they took the plunder, because there was so much of it.
On the fourth day they gathered in the Valley of Blessing, because there they blessed the Lord their God. For this reason that place has been called Blessing to this day.
All the people of Judah returned to Jerusalem, with Jehoshaphat at their head. They came to Jerusalem with great joy, because the Lord had made them rejoice over their enemies.
They came to Jerusalem with songs of praise, lyres, and curved and straight horns, and they came to the house of the Lord.
The fear of the Lord fell upon all the cities and their kingdoms when they heard that the Lord was fighting against Israel’s enemies.
Jehoshaphat's kingdom was at rest from [?], and God gave him rest from all his neighbors.
Jehoshaphat became king over Judah. He was thirty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned in Jerusalem for twenty-five years. His mother’s name was Arubah daughter of Shilhi.
He followed all the ways of his father Asa and did not turn away from them, doing what was right before the Lord.
However, he did not remove the high places, which remained until then, and the people did not set their hearts on the God of their ancestors.
The rest of Jehoshaphat’s deeds, from first to last, are written in the accounts of Jehu son of Hanan, which are recorded in the Book of the Kings of Israel.
After these things, Jehoshaphat king of Judah allied himself with Ahaziah king of Israel, that wicked man who did more evil than all the kings of Israel.
He allied himself with him to build ships to sail to Tarshish, and he built ships in the city of Ezion-geber.

Eliezer son of Dodah, in the city of Mareshah, prophesied against Jehoshaphat and said to him, “Because of your partnership with Ahaziah, the Lord has ruined all your work.” The ships were wrecked, and he could not go to Tarshish.
Jehoshaphat rested with his ancestors and was buried beside his ancestors in the City of David. His son Jehoram succeeded him as king.
He had brothers, sons of Jehoshaphat, whose names were Azariah, Nahuiel, Zechariah, Azariah, Malchiel, and Shephatiah. All these were sons of Jehoshaphat king of Judah.
Their father gave them many gifts: silver, gold, many other gifts, and fortified cities in Judah. But the kingdom was given to Jehoram because he was his oldest son.
Jehoram took over his father’s kingdom and strengthened his position. He killed all his brothers in battle, and he also killed some of the elders of Israel.
He was thirty-two years old when he became king, and he reigned in Jerusalem for eight years.
He followed the ways of the kings of Israel, just as the house of Ahab had done, because Ahab’s sister was his wife. He did what was evil before the Lord.
But the Lord was unwilling to destroy the house of David because of the oath he had sworn to David, to give him and his descendants a shining lamp for all time.
In his days the Edomites rebelled against Judah's rule and appointed a king over themselves.
Jehoram crossed over with his commanders and all his chariots with him. When he rose at night, they struck down the Edomites, and the commanders of the chariots came to him.

The Edomites rebelled against Judah’s rule and have remained independent to this day. At that time the Edomites living in Libnah also rebelled against his rule, because he had abandoned the Lord, the God of his ancestors.
He also made high places in the hill country of Judah, gave wine to the Nazirites of Jerusalem to drink, and scattered the house of Judah.

A message came to him from Elijah the prophet, who said to him, “This is what the LORD, the God of your father David, says: Because you have not followed the ways of your father Jehoshaphat or the ways of Asa king of Judah,

but have followed the ways of the kings of Israel and led Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem astray through the prostitution of the house of Ahab, and have also killed your brothers, your father’s sons, who were better than you,
the Lord is about to strike you, your people, your children, your wives, and all your possessions with a great blow.
you will die of a severe illness and perish in great torment, until your intestines come out because of your illness, and for many years you will languish in torment.”
The Lord will stir up against Joram the spirit of the Philistines and of the Arabs who live among the Indians.

They will come up against Judah and devastate them, and carry away everything found in the king’s palace as plunder, including his sons and his wives. No male child will be left to him except Ahaziah, his youngest son.
After all these things, a disease will strike his intestines, and he will die of a severe illness, with no cure for him.

After many days, when the prophet’s word was fulfilled at the end of two years, his intestines came out because of his illness, and he died of a dreadful disease. The people did not honor him as they had honored his ancestors.

He was thirty-two years old when he became king, and he reigned in Jerusalem for eight years. He departed without being mourned and was buried in the city of his father David, but not in the tombs of the kings.

The inhabitants of Jerusalem made his son Ahaziah king after him, because the raiding force had killed all the older sons when the Arabs came and destroyed the camps. So Ahaziah son of Jehoram became king of Judah.
Ahaziah was twenty-two years old when he became king, and he reigned in Jerusalem for one year. His mother’s name was Athaliah, daughter of Omri.
He followed the ways of the house of Ahab, because he was Ahab’s nephew, and he too sinned greatly.
He did evil before the LORD, like the house of Ahab, because after his father died they became his advisers, to his destruction.
Because he followed their advice, he went with Joram son of Ahab, king of Israel, to wage war against Hazael king of Edom at Ramoth-gilead, and the Edomites wounded Joram.

He returned to Jezreel to recover from the wounds they had inflicted on him at Ramoth when he fought against Hazael king of Edom. Ahaziah went down to see Joram son of Ahab in Jezreel because he was ill.
Ahaziah’s downfall through his coming to Joram was from the LORD. When he arrived, he went out with Joram to meet Jehu son of Nimshi, whom the LORD had anointed to destroy the house of Ahab.
Then, as Jehu was carrying out judgment against the house of Ahab, he found the officials of Judah and the sons of Ahaziah’s brothers, who were serving Ahaziah, and killed them.

He searched for Ahaziah and captured him while he was hiding in Samaria. He had him brought to him, killed him, and buried him, because he said, “He is a descendant of Jehoshaphat, who prayed to the LORD with all his heart.” The house of Ahaziah had no one with the strength to support the kingdom.
When Athaliah, Ahaziah’s mother, saw that her son was dead, she rose up and destroyed all the king’s sons of the house of Judah.

But Jehosheba, the king’s daughter, took Joash son of Ahaziah and stole him away from among the king’s sons who were being killed. She hid him and his nurse in her bedroom. Jehosheba, daughter of King Joram and wife of Jehoiada the priest, hid him from Athaliah because she was Ahaziah’s sister, and they did not kill him.
He remained hidden with her in the house of the Lord for six years, while Athaliah ruled over the land.

In the seventh year Jehoiada took courage and brought together the commanders of hundreds: Azariah son of Jeroham, Ishmael son of Johanan, Azariah son of Obed, Shemaiah son of Iddo, and Elishaphat son of Zichri. All these entered into an oath,
to travel throughout Judah. He gathered the Levites from all the towns of Judah and the heads of the ancestral families of Israel, and they came to Jerusalem.
All the people swore an oath in the house of the LORD before the king. He said to them, “Look, the king’s son will reign over you, as the LORD promised his servant David.
This is what you must do: half of you—the priests, Levites, and gatekeepers coming on duty on the Sabbath—
and a third at the king’s palace, and a third at the Butchers’ Gate. All the people are to keep watch in the courtyard of the house of the Lord.
No one is to enter the house of the LORD except the priests and the Levites. They may enter because they are holy, and all the people are to keep watch over the house of the LORD.
The Levites are to go out with the king, surrounding him, each man with his weapons in his hand. Anyone who enters the inner house must die. Stay with the king when he comes in and when he goes out.”

The Levites and all the people of Judah did as Jehoiada the priest had commanded them. Each man brought his companions, those who kept watch at the beginning of the Sabbath together with those who kept watch at the end of the Sabbath, because Jehoiada the priest had released them from their watches.
Jehoiada the priest gave the commanders of hundreds the spears, small shields, and large shields of King David that were in the house of the LORD.
All the people took their positions, each beside the left side of the house, and by the altar and the house, and they surrounded the king.
They brought out the king's son, placed a crown and a necklace on his head, and made him king. Jehoiada and his sons anointed him and said, “Long live the king!”
Athaliah heard the sound of the people rejoicing and praising the king, and she came to the king at the house of the Lord.

She looked, and there was the king standing by the pillar, according to the custom of kings. Curved and straight horns were sounding before the king, and all the people were rejoicing, sounding horns, and singing praises. Athaliah tore her clothes and said, “Treason! Treason!”

Jehoiada the priest commanded the commanders of hundreds who were in charge of the army, saying to them, “Bring her outside the ranks, and let anyone who follows her be killed with the sword.” For the priest had said, “She must not die in the LORD's house.”
They made room for her, and she went along the road to the horses’ entrance and died there.
Jehoiada swore an oath between himself, all the people, and the king, that they would be the Lord’s people.
All the people of Israel entered the temple of Baal and demolished it. They thoroughly smashed its altars and crushed its images, and they killed the priest of Baal before the altar.

Jehoiada appointed officials in the LORD's house, along with the priests and Levites whom David had divided into groups to guard the LORD's house and offer burnt offerings, as written in the law of Moses, with rejoicing and songs of praise according to David's directions.
The gatekeepers were to stand at the gates of the house of the Lord, so that no unclean people would enter there.
The commanders of hundreds, the rulers of the people, and all the people of the land took him and came through the upper gate of the royal palace. They seated the king on the royal throne.
All the people of the land rejoiced and sounded horns in praise, and they killed Athaliah with the sword.
Joash was seven years old when he became king, and he reigned in Jerusalem for forty years. His mother's name was Zibiah, from the city of Beersheba.
Joash did what was right before the Lord throughout the lifetime of Jehoiada the priest.
Jehoiada took two wives for him, and he fathered sons and daughters.
After these things, Joash privately resolved to restore the LORD's house and repair everything in it that needed attention.

Jehoiada gathered the priests and Levites and said to them, “Go out to the towns of Judah and collect silver and gold from all the towns of Israel. Repair the house of your God year after year, and hurry to complete the work.”

The king summoned Jehoiada the elder and said to him, “Why do you not require the Levites to go and bring from Judah and Jerusalem the offerings of Moses, the LORD's servant?” And they assembled Israel for the tent of meeting.
Athaliah had been teaching the children wickedness, and she broke into the LORD's house. She even made all the holy people who were in the LORD's house into worshippers of idols.
The king gave the command, and they made a chest and placed it outside the gate of the house of the Lord.
They made a proclamation in Judah and Jerusalem that people should bring to the LORD the contribution that Moses, the LORD's servant, had commanded in the wilderness.
All the officials and all the people rejoiced and brought their contributions. They made a chest, set it in place, and put their contributions into it until it was full.
When they saw that there was a great deal of silver in the chest, the king's secretary and the chief steward of the high priest came in, counted the silver, and tied it into bags.
They gave it to those doing the work on the LORD's house. They hired stonecutters and carpenters to repair the LORD's house, as well as workers in iron and bronze to repair the LORD's house.
Jehoiada grew old and lived a full life, and he died at the age of one hundred and thirty.

They buried him in the City of David, in the tombs of the kings, and said, “This is how someone who has done good in Israel should be rewarded, someone who has also made great efforts for the LORD's house.”
After Jehoiada died, the leaders of Judah came and bowed down to the king, because he listened to them.
They abandoned the house of the LORD, the God of their ancestors, and went and served images and idols. Wrath came upon Judah and Jerusalem because they had committed this sin.
He sent messages to them through prophets to turn them back from their ways, but they did not listen. He warned them, but they would not accept it.

The Spirit of the LORD clothed Zechariah son of Jehoiada the priest. He went up and stood above the people and said to them, “This is what the LORD says: Why have you transgressed the LORD's commandments? You will not prosper. Because you have abandoned my way, I too am abandoning you.”
They rebelled against him and stoned him at the king’s command in the courtyard of the LORD’s house.

King Joash did not acknowledge the kindness that Jehoiada the priest, their father, had shown him, and after Jehoiada's death he killed his sons. As his sons were being killed, they said, “May the LORD see and demand an accounting!”
At the end of the year, the army of Edom came up against him and attacked Judah and Jerusalem. They destroyed all the leaders of the people and sent all their plunder to the king at Damascus.

Although only a few men had come with the army of Edom, the LORD handed over a very large army to them, because they had abandoned the LORD, the God of their ancestors. The judges condemned what Joash had done.

When they withdrew from him, they left him severely ill. His servants plotted against him because of the blood of the sons of Jehoiada the priest. They killed him on his bed, and he died. They buried him in the city of his ancestor David, but they did not bury him in the tombs of the kings.
These are the names of the men who plotted against him: Zabur son of Shimeath, an Ammonite woman, and Jehozabar son of Natrath, a Moabite woman.

As for his sons, the many people who plotted against him, and the rest of the sins he committed in the LORD's house, they are written in the explanations of the Book of Kings. His son Amaziah became king after him.
Amaziah was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned in Jerusalem for twenty-nine years. His mother's name was Jehoaddan, from Jerusalem.
He did what was right before the LORD, but not with an undivided heart.
When his hold on the kingdom became strong, he killed the servants who had killed his father the king.

He did not kill the murderers' children, because it is written in the book of the law of Moses, as the LORD commanded: “Fathers must not die because of their children, and children must not die because of their fathers. Each person must die for his own sins.”

Amaziah assembled the people of Judah and organized them by their ancestral families under commanders of thousands and commanders of hundreds, throughout Judah and Benjamin. He counted those twenty years old and older and found three hundred thousand young men ready to go to war, who could draw swords and carry shields.
He also hired one hundred thousand mighty warriors from Israel for one hundred talents of silver.
The LORD's prophet came to him and said to the king, “Do not let the whole army of Israel go with you, because the LORD is not with all Israel or with any of the people of Ephraim.
For you are going in to wage a great battle, but the LORD will throw you down before your enemies, because you have not praised the LORD, who is the helper and the one who raises up.”

Amaziah said to the LORD's prophet, “What folly have I committed in giving these hundred talents to the men of Israel?” God's prophet said to him, “Your Lord and God can give you much more than this, many times what you have given.”

Amaziah dismissed the men who had come to him from Ephraim, sending them back to their own place. His anger grew very fierce against the people of Israel, and he sent them back to their own place in his furious anger.
Amaziah took courage, led his people out, and went to the Valley of Salt. He killed and destroyed ten thousand of the people of Mount Gebal.
The people of Judah captured ten thousand alive, and they were brought to the top of the rock. They all came bound in chains.

The warriors whom Amaziah had taken captive when he went to battle were given authority by him over the towns of Judah, among the Samaritans, and over the towns of the nations. They killed three thousand in those towns and took a great deal of plunder.

After Amaziah came back, having turned to devastate the Edomites, they brought him the gods of the people of Mount Gebal. He set them up before him, bowed down before them, and offered them fragrant incense.
The LORD became angry with Amaziah and sent a prophet to him, who said, “Why have you prayed before the gods of the nations, who could not rescue their worshipers from your hands?”

While the prophet was speaking with him, he said to him, “The worship of wooden idols has been granted to the king.” The prophet withdrew from him and said, “Woe to you! The LORD has devised an evil plan against you to destroy you, and you have not listened to me.”
King Amaziah of Judah took counsel and sent word to Joash son of Jehoahaz, son of Jehu, king of Israel, saying, “Come, let us face one another.”

Jehoash king of Israel sent word to Amaziah king of Judah, saying, “The thistle in Lebanon sent word to the cedar in Lebanon, saying, ‘Give your daughter to my son as his wife.’ But a wild animal in Lebanon passed by and trampled the thistle.

You have indeed devastated the Edomites, and because of this your heart has become proud. Enjoy your honor and stay at home. Why are you craving disaster, so that you and the people of Judah with you should fall?”
But Amaziah would not listen.
Joash king of Israel went up, and they went up and faced one another at Beth-shemesh, a town within the territory of Judah.
